findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.brief: q2.reconnectDoesNotBackfillHost asserts a host reconnect has no mechanism analogous to the guest's cursor-resumable backfill, because the connect omits lastSeq.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.measured: bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:947-1010 derives role from verifiedPlayerId === entry.hostPlayerId, and the role === 'host' arm calls entry.syncSession.joinMember(...) UNCONDITIONALLY - it never reads envelope.lastSeq. CampaignSyncSession.joinMember (:435-497) always sends buildBaselineEvent (:764-791) followed by the tail after that revision. The envelope.lastSeq !== undefined resync arm (:1082-1122) sits on the guest / room-code path only.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.consequence: What actually makes a host reconnect backfill is H1 folding the hydration BASELINE, not H2's cursor. For a GM who IS the registered host, H2 changes nothing on the wire. H2 still earns its place for the D9 case the brief itself cites: a GM connecting from another device is not the registered host, is routed down the guest / replica arm, and that arm is cursor-driven.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.claimDiscipline: This artefact does NOT claim H2 fixes host reconnect backfill. H1 does.

findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.brief: q2.reusableProjectionFn says applyAuthoritativeStateToGuestCampaign is reusable for the host's own view with no modification.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.measured: Its buildFactionStandings REBUILT campaign.factionStandings from the ledger's Record<string, number>. IFactionStanding (src/types/campaign/factionStanding/IFactionStanding.ts:63-72) also carries accoladeLevel, censureLevel, lastChangeDate and history, none of which the ledger round-trips. Reusing it unmodified on the host would have silently erased them from the host's own richer record.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.consequence: The projection now MERGES: regard and the derived level update in place, everything else on an existing standing is kept, and a fresh entry is seeded only for a faction the record has never seen. Pinned by the row 'keeps standing metadata the ledger cannot carry when it folds'. Guest behavior is unchanged in practice - a guest mirror never held that metadata.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.claimDiscipline: Information loss prevented inline rather than filed, per the pending-task file-decision rubric.

findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.brief: The H1 charter suggested reusing useCampaignMirrorStore's applyEvent/applySnapshot with a host-scoped instance.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.measured: useCampaignMirrorStore is a zustand singleton with no factory, and it is read by CampaignCoopEntryPanel and by the surface's own guest-only guestMirrorSummary; populating it from the host would have made a host look like a guest mirror. A second host store would have been exactly the duplication the tasks.md preamble rejected.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.consequence: The fold rules were extracted to pure functions instead and the mirror store delegates to them. The host holds its fold in a component ref.
findingsCorrectingTheAdmissionBrief.deliberateNonSymmetry: The host's fold is component-scoped while the guest's mirror store is module-scoped. This is intentional and commented at the ref: the baseline frame is stamped sequence -1, and the shared adopt rule pins such a frame to cursor 0, so a host returning with a held cursor above 0 would REJECT its own hydration baseline and backfill nothing. Starting empty makes every host reconnect converge completely.

fR1Disclosure.title: An in-mount reconnect rejects the server's own hydration baseline
fR1Disclosure.severity: MEDIUM (disclosure; no code change in this slice)
fR1Disclosure.mechanism: The host effect's dep array is [campaignId, coopMode, matchId, roomCode, store]. A roomCode change (invite rotation) or a matchId change re-runs the effect - tearing down and reopening the transport - WITHOUT unmounting, so the hostFold ref survives at whatever cursor it reached. The server hydrates every host (re)connection with buildBaselineEvent stamped sequence -1 (CampaignSyncSession.ts:779); foldCampaignFrame pins such a frame to cursor 0 (campaignAuthoritativeFold.ts:118-121); foldCampaignSnapshot then rejects it because adopted (0) < fold.lastSequence (campaignAuthoritativeFold.ts:74-76). The baseline is exactly what carries the commits that landed during the socket gap, so those commits are dropped and the live tail resumes on a fold that is missing them.
fR1Disclosure.proof: Reviewer PROBE-1: mount a host, fold to cursor 7, re-render with a rotated room code, emit a baseline at revision 9 carrying balance 123456. Result: Expected 123456, Received 700000 - the baseline was rejected. Probe reverted; reviewer worktree clean.
fR1Disclosure.notARegression: Before this slice the host never updated at all, so this narrows the defect rather than widening it.
fR1Disclosure.probability: LOW. The window is the GM's own socket reopen, triggered only by an invite rotation or a matchId change, and the GM is the party committing - so the commits most likely to fall in the gap are the GM's own, which the GM has just issued. It resolves on the next full mount.
fR1Disclosure.whyNotFixedHere: Both candidate fixes reach outside this slice. Resetting the fold on effect re-run would defeat H2's cursor entirely. Making a sequence -1 baseline an unconditional replace changes the SHARED guest semantics: the same adopt-at-0 rule is what the guest mirror relies on for its own large-gap resync, so the change would need a red-first row on both roles, not a host-only edit. Either is its own slice.
fR1Disclosure.namedInCode: src/components/campaign/coop/CampaignCoopRouteSurfaceConnected.tsx, the hostFold ref comment, as of commit 5973dc7fb.
